text: The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, I was in the citadel of Susa.

versions.text: The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, while I was in the citadel of Susa,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew of verse 1 is a complete clause ("and I was in the citadel of Susa"); rendering it as a dependent "while" clause leaves verse 1 as a sentence fragment, which is awkward for oral reading. Note also the name is usually spelled Hacaliah/Hakaliah — consistent spelling is fine, but the fragment should be resolved.

text: Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some men from Judah, and I questioned them about the Jews who had survived, those left from the exile, and about Jerusalem.
They told me, "Those who survived the exile and remain in the province are in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire."
When I heard these words, I sat down and wept. For days I mourned, fasting and praying before the God of heaven.

versions.text: When I heard this, I sat down and wept. For days I mourned, fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
versions.explanation: "Ha-devarim ha-elleh" is plural, "these words" or "these things"; "this" slightly flattens the Hebrew and loses the link with "the words of Nehemiah" in verse 1.

text: I said: "LORD, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps his covenant of steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments,

let your ear be attentive and your eyes open to hear the prayer of your servant, which I pray before you today, day and night, for your servants, the people of Israel. I confess the sins we Israelites have committed against you. Both I and my father's house have sinned.

versions.text: let your ear be attentive and your eyes open to hear the prayer of your servant, which I now pray before you day and night for your servants, the people of Israel. I confess the sins we Israelites have committed against you. Both I and my father's house have sinned.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has both "today" (hayyom) and "day and night"; the current rendering collapses these into "now," losing an element of the text.

text: We have acted corruptly toward you and have not kept the commandments, statutes, and ordinances you gave your servant Moses.
Remember, I pray, the word you commanded your servant Moses: 'If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations;

but if you return to me and keep my commandments and do them, then even if your exiles are at the farthest horizon, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place I have chosen as a dwelling for my name.'
They are your servants and your people, whom you redeemed by your great power and your mighty hand.

Lord, let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant and to the prayer of your servants who delight in revering your name. Grant your servant success today, and give him compassion in the presence of this man." I was the king's cupbearer.
